transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... man, ever since I moved into that busted-up room a few weeks ago, everything's just falling apart. I'm snapping at people left and right. And I'm up half the night trying to fix leaks or get the heat working. You know, my uncle used to do HVAC, and he always said you gotta check the pilot light first, but this thing is so old it doesn't even have a normal pilot light. It's like something out of the 1950s. Anyway, because I'm up all night messing with that, I'm dragging myself into work late. I do construction, mostly framing and drywall right now, and I'm messing up stuff I normally handle with my eyes closed. Dropped a whole stack of two-by-fours yesterday because my head was just... somewhere else. My foreman, Dave, he's a good guy, but he's got this truck, a Ford F-150, that he's always talking about getting lifted, and he was yelling at me from the cab of it while I was trying to pick up the wood. So yeah, I just... I can't keep going like this.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

I don't know if I'd say depressed, exactly. I just... I don't really care about much right now. Like, I usually like working on my truck on the weekends, you know? It's a '98 Chevy Silverado. Got it for a steal from this guy a couple towns over. He thought the transmission was shot, but it was really just a bad solenoid. Took me like two hours to swap it out. But lately, I just look at it sitting in the driveway and I don't even want to touch it. Needs an oil change bad, too. I always use full synthetic, Mobil 1 usually, because my buddy Mike swears by it. Mike's the guy who helped me put the new exhaust on it last summer. We were out there till like 2 AM... but yeah, I just haven't had the energy for it. Or for much of anything, really.
How long have you been feeling this way, where you don’t care about much and don’t have energy for things you usually enjoy?

I guess... probably about a month? It pretty much started right after I moved into that room over in Bridgeport. Which, man, I don't even know why I picked that neighborhood. The parking is a total joke. I had to park my Silverado like four blocks away the day I moved in. And carrying all my stuff... I got these heavy-duty boxes from the back of the Home Depot, the ones they use for shipping the big power tools, because my buddy works receiving there. He's always hooking me up with stuff like that. But anyway, carrying those boxes four blocks was brutal. And then I got a parking ticket my second day there because the street sweeping sign is completely rusted out. You literally can't even read the days on it. I tried fighting the ticket on the city website, but the whole system kept crashing on my phone. But yeah... it's been about a month of just feeling like this, ever since I got to that place.
Have you had days where you feel down or low most of the time, even before this move happened, and if so, how often has that been happening over the past couple of years?

No, not really. Before I moved into this place, I was actually doing pretty good. I mean, the past couple of years have been fine. Like, two years ago I was working on this massive commercial site out by the highway, doing steel framing. Man, steel framing is a whole different beast than wood. You gotta use these self-tapping screws, and if you don't have a good impact driver, you're basically out of luck. I had this Dewalt 20-volt, the XR brushless one. Best drill I ever owned until some guy walked off with it at a Wawa parking lot. I left it in the bed of my truck for literally two minutes while I went in to get a meatball sub. Wawa makes a pretty decent meatball sub, honestly, especially if you get the provolone melted on it and add a little bit of oregano. But man, I was so mad about that drill. I had to go to Lowe's and buy a whole new kit, and they didn't even have the hard case for it anymore, just those cheap canvas bags that rip after a month on the site. But... wait, what were you asking? Oh, feeling low? Yeah, no, I was totally fine back then. It's really just been since I got this new room that everything went sideways.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things that you used to find pleasurable, like working on your truck or spending time with friends?

Yeah, I mean, like I was saying with the Silverado... I just don't even want to look at it. And as for hanging out, my buddy Mike actually texted me on Tuesday wanting to go to Miller's Ale House to watch the game. They do this special on Tuesdays, these things called Zingers. Basically just boneless wings, but they bread them differently, I don't know. I usually get the garlic parmesan ones with a side of fries. 

The last time we were there, the waitress actually dropped a whole pitcher of Bud Light right on this guy's boots at the table next to us. He was wearing Timberland Pros, the steel-toe ones. I wear those on the job site sometimes, they're alright, but I actually prefer Red Wings if I have the cash. Takes like a solid month to break them in, though. You gotta use mink oil on the leather or you'll get these massive blisters on your heels, right where the back stitching is. It's the worst when you're carrying drywall all day and your heels are just peeling. 

But... yeah, I didn't even text Mike back. I just didn't feel like going out or talking to anybody. So, yeah, I guess I'm just not really into any of my usual stuff right now.
Have you had days where you feel down or low most of the time, not just for a few hours here and there, and if so, how often has that happened in the past month?

I don't know if I'd say I feel sad or low, really. It's not like I'm sitting around crying or anything. I just... I don't do anything. Like this past Sunday, I just sat on the edge of my bed staring at the TV for hours. I didn't even have it turned on. Which is a waste, because I just bought this new Vizio soundbar from Walmart right before I moved. The one with the wireless subwoofer. 

You gotta put the subwoofer in the corner of the room if you want the bass to actually bounce off the walls right. My old roommate used to put his right next to the couch and it sounded terrible, it just rattled the springs in the cushions. I tried telling him, but he was one of those guys who thinks he knows everything because he watched a YouTube video once. He tried to wire his own aftermarket headlights on his Honda Civic and completely fried the wiring harness. Cost him like eight hundred bucks to get a real mechanic to fix it. I told him he should have just bought the plug-and-play ones, but whatever. 

But, uh... wait. What did you ask me? Down or low? Yeah, no, I don't really feel sad most of the time. Just kind of... blank, I guess. Like I just don't care.
Have you noticed that you’ve been doing less or less than you used to in your daily life, like skipping tasks or not keeping up with things you normally would?

Yeah, I guess I have been letting things slide a lot. Especially at work. My foreman actually pulled me aside and told me I could lose my shot at moving toward crew lead if I keep slipping. I’ve already had a bunch of problems with my work paperwork and messing up the scheduling because of all this. 

Which, honestly, the scheduling is all done on this app on our phones now, and it's a total pain anyway. You gotta clock in and out on it, but if you don't have a good signal out on the site, the little loading circle just spins and spins. We were working out at this new subdivision past the county line last week, and I swear, there is zero cell service out there. You have to walk all the way over to the porta-johns just to get one bar. And those porta-johns, man, when the sun beats down on them all afternoon? It's literally like a sauna in there. The blue chemical stuff they put in the bottom gets so hot it actually smells like burning plastic. The guys were complaining to the super about getting them cleaned out more than once a week, but you know how these big companies are, they just want to save a few bucks wherever they can. Like a couple months ago, they switched our work gloves from the good thick leather ones to these cheap synthetic ones that practically melt if you're grinding metal or doing any hot work... 

But, uh... wait, yeah. I just haven't been keeping up with my end of things. The paperwork and everything. My foreman is definitely noticing that I'm just not on top of it lately.
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or have you felt physically slowed down most days?

Slowly? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not doing much these days, but when I do move, it's just my regular speed. Definitely not as slow as this guy Gary on our crew, anyway. I swear that guy moves in actual slow motion. He's this older dude, always wears these bright neon green suspenders for some reason. 

He mostly just runs the skid steer, which is fine, but when he actually has to get out of the cab to help us move materials, it takes him like ten minutes just to climb down. We have a Bobcat T76 on site, the track loader one. It's actually a pretty sweet machine, way better than the wheeled ones if you're working in mud. The wheeled ones just spin out and get stuck the second it rains. Last spring we had this massive downpour and one of the new guys buried a wheeled John Deere loader straight up to the axles. We had to get an excavator just to pull him out, and we actually snapped a heavy-duty tow strap right in half doing it. It sounded like a literal gunshot when it snapped. You gotta be so careful with those straps, man, because if they snap and whip back at you, it'll break your leg easy. Or worse. My uncle actually lost his back window in his Chevy because a strap let go and the metal hook went right through the glass...

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Me moving slow? Yeah, no, my body feels fine. I'm just sitting around a lot more, that's all.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy *any* activities at all lately — even things that used to make you feel good, like spending time with friends or eating your favorite food?

No, I still enjoy things sometimes. Like, a good meal still tastes good, you know? I actually went to this taco truck down by the old armory a couple days ago. Best al pastor I've had in a long time. 

The guy who runs it is from Oaxaca, I think. He has this massive trompo set up right in the window, and he slices the pork right off it while it's spinning. He uses a real pineapple on top, too, none of that canned stuff. Canned pineapple is just way too sweet, it completely ruins the balance of the marinade. My ex-girlfriend used to put canned pineapple on her pizza, which, whatever, people like Hawaiian pizza, but she would put barbecue sauce on it instead of tomato sauce. It was the grossest thing I ever tasted. She'd order it from Domino's every Friday night, and I'd always just end up making myself a sandwich. I actually make a really good Italian sub. You gotta use the hard salami, not the cheap stuff, and you have to shred the lettuce super fine, like they do at Jersey Mike's. If you just put whole leaves of lettuce on a sub, it slides all over the place when you take a bite and makes a huge mess. Plus, you gotta hit it with the oil and vinegar right on the bread before you put the meat on...

But, uh... wait. Enjoying things? Yeah, I still like some things. I just don't have the energy to go do them much, but when I do, it's fine.
Have you had any days in the past month where you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day?

Down or hopeless? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm stressed out about the breakup and everything, and work is a mess, but I'm not, like, hopeless. I just feel kind of stuck right now, you know? Like I'm spinning my tires in the mud. 

Speaking of mud, you should have seen the site yesterday. We had that rain over the weekend, and the whole foundation trench for lot 42 completely washed out. The super was losing his mind. He had us out there with shovels trying to dig out the forms before the concrete trucks showed up. Mud is the absolute worst thing to shovel, man. It sticks to the metal, so every time you lift a scoop, it weighs like fifty pounds, and then half of it doesn't even slide off when you throw it. You have to keep banging the shovel against a rock just to clear it. I actually bought this special shovel a while back, a fiberglass handle one with a non-stick coating on the blade. Cost me like sixty bucks at Home Depot, which is insane for a shovel, but I figured it was an investment, right? Well, the very first week I brought it to the site, some idiot ran over the handle with a skid steer and snapped it clean in half. I was so mad. And of course, nobody fessed up to doing it. Just found it lying in the dirt next to the framing lumber...

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Hopeless? Yeah, no, I don't feel hopeless. Just, you know, dealing with a lot right now. I'm not down like that all the time.
Have you found yourself not getting things done at work, home, or in other areas of life because you just don’t feel motivated or interested in doing them?

Not getting things done? I mean, I guess I'm a little behind on some stuff, but it's not like I don't care. I'm just tired. Like, my apartment is a bit of a mess right now, but I'll get to it. I just haven't felt like doing laundry, mostly. 

Laundry is such a scam anyway, man. You pay like two-fifty to wash, and then another two-fifty to dry, and the dryers at my complex don't even work right. You have to run them twice just to get a load of jeans dry. I complained to the landlord about it, this guy Mr. Henderson. He's always wearing these golf shirts that are way too tight, and he just brushed me off. Said I was putting too many clothes in at once. Like, buddy, I know how to do laundry. My mom taught me how to separate the colors and everything. She used to be super strict about it. If a red sock got in with the whites, she'd lose her mind. She used this special stain remover spray that smelled like straight up chemicals, but it got everything out. I tried to find it at Target once, but I think they stopped making it because it probably caused cancer or something. Everything causes cancer now, right? I read this article online that said even the non-stick coating on pans is toxic. Which sucks, because I make eggs every morning. Well, not every morning lately, but I usually do. You gotta cook 'em low and slow if you want good scrambled eggs. If you blast the heat, they just get rubbery and gross. I usually throw some cheddar cheese in there, maybe some hot sauce...

But, uh... wait. What were we talking about? Motivation? Yeah, I mean, I'm doing okay. Just a little behind on chores, but I'm not, like, completely ignoring my life or anything. Work is still getting done, even if I'm not thrilled about being there.
Have you found that nothing really gives you pleasure anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

Pleasure? No, I wouldn't say nothing gives me pleasure. I mean, I was just talking about those tacos, right? And I still like watching the game on Sundays. Though honestly, the refs this season have been absolute garbage. Did you see that holding call in the fourth quarter on Sunday? Total phantom call. The guy barely touched the jersey, and the ref throws the flag from like forty yards away. It completely killed the drive. My buddy Steve was over, and he actually threw his beer can at the TV. Luckily it was empty, but it still dented the screen a little bit. Steve gets way too worked up about football. He plays in like three different fantasy leagues and he's always checking his phone during the game, complaining about how his tight end isn't getting enough targets. I tried doing fantasy football one year, but it's just too much work. You have to check the injury reports every week, and deal with the waiver wire... it's basically a second job. And my actual job is exhausting enough. Speaking of which, Steve owes me twenty bucks from a bet we made on the preseason, and he keeps dodging me about it. Like, dude, it's twenty bucks, just pay up. I know he has it, because he just bought this massive new truck. One of those F-250s with the lifted suspension. It's ridiculous, he doesn't even haul anything, he just drives it to his office job. Getting in and out of that thing is a workout...

But, uh... wait, what was the question? Nothing giving me pleasure? Yeah, no, I still enjoy stuff. I'm just, you know, tired a lot. But I still like things.
Have you experienced days where absolutely nothing seemed enjoyable or interesting to you, even things you usually care about?

No, I don't think so. I mean, there hasn't been a day where literally *nothing* was interesting. Like, even on a bad day, I can still get into a good YouTube rabbit hole, you know? I was watching these videos the other night about guys restoring rusty tools. It's crazy what they can do. They take this axe head that looks like it's been buried in a swamp for a hundred years, and they soak it in vinegar, scrub it down, and polish it until it looks brand new. Then they carve a custom handle for it out of hickory or ash or something. I actually tried to carve a piece of wood once when I was a kid. My grandpa gave me this little pocket knife—an Old Timer, I think it was called. It had three different blades. I was sitting on the back porch trying to whittle a stick into a spear, and I ended up slicing my thumb open. Bled like crazy. My grandma freaked out and poured hydrogen peroxide all over it, which stung so bad. She always used peroxide for everything. Scraped knee? Peroxide. Bee sting? Peroxide. She even used it to clean the bathroom grout, which actually worked pretty well. The bathroom always smelled like a hospital, though. 

But, uh... what were you asking? Days where nothing is enjoyable? No, I haven't had that. I mean, I'm stressed, but I still find stuff to do.
Have you noticed that your mood has been low nearly every day for most of the day, even when there’s no obvious reason for it?

Low mood every day? Nah, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I get bummed out sometimes, especially with everything going on lately, but it's not like an all-day, every-day kind of thing. Like, yesterday I was actually in a pretty decent mood because we finally finished framing out that new house on the west side. Took us forever because the lumber delivery got delayed twice. 

Man, dealing with those supply companies is a nightmare right now. You order two-by-fours and they show up looking like hockey sticks, they're so warped. My boss, Gary, he was screaming at the delivery driver on Tuesday. The driver's just this kid, probably barely eighteen, looking terrified. I felt bad for him, so I gave him a Gatorade from my cooler. It was the blue kind. Cool Blue, I think it's called? Best flavor by far. Though the yellow one is okay if you're really hungover. Not that I drink much anymore, but back when I was eighteen, me and my buddies used to drink those cheap 40-ounce malt liquors. We'd hang out behind the old abandoned roller rink... they tore it down a couple years ago to build a strip mall. Now there's a mattress store there. Who buys that many mattresses? There's a mattress store on like every corner. It's gotta be a front for something, right? Like money laundering or whatever. I saw this documentary on Netflix about money laundering... 

But, uh... what was I saying? Oh, being down all the time. No, I don't think so. I'm just stressed out, you know? But I still have okay days.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt a loss of pleasure or interest in nearly all activities for most of the day, nearly every day?

Loss of pleasure for most of the day? Nah, I don't think so. I mean, I told you about the YouTube videos, right? I still watch those. And I still like hanging out with my dog, Buster. He's a good boy. A pitbull mix, I think. I found him wandering around the job site a couple years ago, looking all skinny and pathetic. He was trying to eat a discarded piece of drywall. I gave him half my turkey sandwich, and he just followed me around the rest of the day. My boss tried to chase him off, but Buster just hid under my truck. I took him home that night, and he's been with me ever since. He's got this weird habit, though. Every time the mail carrier comes, he doesn't bark, he just sits by the window and whines. Like a really high-pitched whine. It's so annoying. I tried training him out of it with those little training treats, the ones that smell like liver? But he just eats the treat and keeps whining. Dogs are weird, man. My neighbor's dog, this little yappy terrier thing, barks at literally everything. A leaf blows across the street? Bark. A squirrel looks at him funny? Bark. I don't know how they deal with it. I'd go crazy. 

But, uh... what did you ask me? Loss of interest? Yeah, no, I still care about stuff. I'm just worn out from work and everything else going on. But I still like doing things.
Have you had days in the past two weeks where you felt like nothing was interesting or enjoyable for most of the day, nearly every day?

Man, I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I said, no, I haven't had days where nothing is enjoyable. I mean, I still like coming home and cracking open a beer on the porch. I usually get those cheap lagers, you know? Like PBR or Miller High Life. People talk trash about cheap beer, but honestly, after sweating on a roof for ten hours, it hits the spot way better than some fancy craft IPA that tastes like pine needles and grapefruit. My buddy Dave, he got super into homebrewing a few years ago. He bought all this equipment—kettles, carboys, hydrometers, the whole nine yards. He set it all up in his garage, which made his wife furious because she couldn't park her car in there during the winter. And winters here get brutal. Last year, we had that ice storm that knocked out the power for three days. I had to sleep in my Carhartt jacket and two pairs of socks. I tried to heat up a can of soup over a candle, which, let me tell you, does not work at all. It just gets the bottom of the can all black and sooty, and the soup stays freezing cold. I ended up just eating it cold anyway. It was chicken noodle. 

But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, enjoying things. No, I still enjoy stuff. I'm just stressed, that's all. Not like... completely dead inside or anything.
Have you felt a noticeable drop in your energy or felt unusually fatigued nearly every day for the past couple of weeks, even when you’re not doing much physically?

Unusually fatigued? Nah, not really. I mean, I'm beat at the end of the day, but I haul lumber and pour concrete for a living. It's not like I'm sitting on a couch feeling tired for no reason. We actually just finished this massive concrete pour on Wednesday. Concrete work is the worst, man. You gotta move so fast before it cures, especially when the sun is beating down on you. 

My coworker, Tommy, he actually dropped his phone right into the wet cement on that job. Just bloop, right in. It was one of those brand new phones too, the ones with the three cameras on the back. He tried to fish it out with his trowel, but it was completely encased by the time he got to it. Looked like a little gray brick. He was so mad he kicked the company truck and dented the fender. Boss was pissed, said he's taking it out of Tommy's paycheck. Which is kind of messed up, because the company trucks are already beat to hell anyway. The one I drive has a radio that only plays static, and the AC smells like old gym socks. I tried spraying Febreze in the vents last week, but it just made it smell like tropical gym socks. I don't even know what tropical is supposed to smell like anyway. Like coconuts? I hate coconut. The texture is awful, it's like chewing on wood shavings. Reminds me of hamster cages. I had a hamster when I was ten, named him Rex. He used to run on that squeaky wheel all night long... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Drop in energy? Yeah, no, my energy is fine. Just regular tired from working, that's all.
Have you had days in the past two weeks where you felt like nothing was interesting or enjoyable for most of the day, nearly every day?

Are you asking me the same thing again? Man, I swear we just talked about this. No, I don't feel like nothing is enjoyable. Like I said, I still enjoy things. I still got my dog, I still got my beer. I mean, speaking of beer, I actually went to the store yesterday to get some, and the line was out the door. Just ridiculous. Turns out the lottery was up to like, what, 800 million or something? Everyone and their mother was buying tickets. I don't get the point, honestly. The odds of winning are worse than getting struck by lightning while getting eaten by a shark. But this one guy in front of me, he bought fifty bucks worth of scratch-offs. Just stood right there at the counter, scratching them with a quarter, holding up the whole line. The cashier looked like she wanted to die. She was this older lady, had those glasses on a chain around her neck, you know? She just kept sighing and looking at the ceiling. I felt bad for her, but I was also just trying to pay for my twelve-pack and go home. My feet were killing me. I need new boots. The steel toe on my left boot is starting to cut into my toes when I kneel down. I tried to find the same brand I bought last time, but the store at the mall closed down. Malls are so dead these days anyway. It's just empty storefronts and those weird kiosks selling phone cases... 

Anyway, look, I'm not sitting around hating everything, okay? I still like doing my usual stuff. I'm just stressed out.
Have you had days in the past two weeks where you felt like nothing was interesting or enjoyable for most of the day, nearly every day?

Dude, are you messing with me right now? You literally just asked me this, like, two seconds ago. And I already told you no, I still enjoy things. I'm not sitting around miserable all day. I mean, I was pretty miserable yesterday when my truck wouldn't start. The starter's been acting up for weeks, making this horrible grinding noise every time I turn the key. Sounds like metal chewing on metal. My buddy Carl told me I could just tap the starter with a hammer to get it going, but you try crawling under a Chevy in a gravel driveway when it's raining sideways. Gravel is the worst. My landlord refuses to pave the driveway. He says it's "rustic," but really he's just cheap. The guy drives a brand new Lexus but won't spend a dime on the property. Last month the hot water heater broke and it took him four days to send a guy out. Four days of taking freezing cold showers before work. It wakes you up, I'll give you that, but it's miserable. The plumber he finally sent was this kid who looked like he was barely out of high school. He had his pants sagging so low you could see his entire boxers. Plumber's crack is one thing, but this was a whole different level. He actually forgot his wrench and had to borrow mine. 

But seriously, doc, how many times are you gonna ask me the same question? No, I don't feel like nothing is enjoyable. Can we talk about something else now?

doctor.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking psychiatric evaluation.
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

target_item.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
target_item.manifestation: I came in because ever since I moved into that busted-up room, I’m snapping at people, staying up fixing leaks or heat, then dragging myself late to work and messing up stuff I normally handle.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the item corresponding to my chief_complaint_symptom_code, which is S081.

patient.answer: Well, I came in because... man, ever since I moved into that busted-up room a few weeks ago, everything's just falling apart. I'm snapping at people left and right. And I'm up half the night trying to fix leaks or get the heat working. You know, my uncle used to do HVAC, and he always said you gotta check the pilot light first, but this thing is so old it doesn't even have a normal pilot light. It's like something out of the 1950s. Anyway, because I'm up all night messing with that, I'm dragging myself into work late. I do construction, mostly framing and drywall right now, and I'm messing up stuff I normally handle with my eyes closed. Dropped a whole stack of two-by-fours yesterday because my head was just... somewhere else. My foreman, Dave, he's a good guy, but he's got this truck, a Ford F-150, that he's always talking about getting lifted, and he was yelling at me from the cab of it while I was trying to pick up the wood. So yeah, I just... I can't keep going like this.

But lately, I just look at it sitting in the driveway and I don't even want to touch it. Needs an oil change bad, too. I always use full synthetic, Mobil 1 usually, because my buddy Mike swears by it. Mike's the guy who helped me put the new exhaust on it last summer. I tried fighting the ticket on the city website, but the whole system kept crashing on my phone. But yeah... it's been about a month of just feeling like this, ever since I got to that place.

You gotta use these self-tapping screws, and if you don't have a good impact driver, you're basically out of luck. I had this Dewalt 20-volt, the XR brushless one. Best drill I ever owned until some guy walked off with it at a Wawa parking lot. I left it in the bed of my truck for literally two minutes while I went in to get a meatball sub. Wawa makes a pretty decent meatball sub, honestly, especially if you get the provolone melted on it and add a little bit of oregano. But man, I was so mad about that drill. I had to go to Lowe's and buy a whole new kit, and they didn't even have the hard case for it anymore, just those cheap canvas bags that rip after a month on the site. But... wait, what were you asking? Oh, feeling low? Yeah, no, I was totally fine back then. It's really just been since I got this new room that everything went sideways.

Yeah, I mean, like I was saying with the Silverado... I just don't even want to look at it. Basically just boneless wings, but they bread them differently, I don't know. I usually get the garlic parmesan ones with a side of fries. 

The last time we were there, the waitress actually dropped a whole pitcher of Bud Light right on this guy's boots at the table next to us. He was wearing Timberland Pros, the steel-toe ones. I wear those on the job site sometimes, they're alright, but I actually prefer Red Wings if I have the cash. Takes like a solid month to break them in, though. You gotta use mink oil on the leather or you'll get these massive blisters on your heels, right where the back stitching is. It's the worst when you're carrying drywall all day and your heels are just peeling. 

But... yeah, I didn't even text Mike back. I just didn't feel like going out or talking to anybody. So, yeah, I guess I'm just not really into any of my usual stuff right now.

I don't know if I'd say I feel sad or low, really. It's not like I'm sitting around crying or anything. I just... I don't do anything. Like this past Sunday, I just sat on the edge of my bed staring at the TV for hours. I didn't even have it turned on. Which is a waste, because I just bought this new Vizio soundbar from Walmart right before I moved. The one with the wireless subwoofer. 

You gotta put the subwoofer in the corner of the room if you want the bass to actually bounce off the walls right. My old roommate used to put his right next to the couch and it sounded terrible, it just rattled the springs in the cushions. I tried telling him, but he was one of those guys who thinks he knows everything because he watched a YouTube video once. He tried to wire his own aftermarket headlights on his Honda Civic and completely fried the wiring harness. Cost him like eight hundred bucks to get a real mechanic to fix it. I told him he should have just bought the plug-and-play ones, but whatever. 

But, uh... wait. What did you ask me? Down or low? Yeah, no, I don't really feel sad most of the time. Just kind of... blank, I guess. Like I just don't care.

Yeah, I guess I have been letting things slide a lot. Especially at work. My foreman actually pulled me aside and told me I could lose my shot at moving toward crew lead if I keep slipping. I’ve already had a bunch of problems with my work paperwork and messing up the scheduling because of all this. 

Which, honestly, the scheduling is all done on this app on our phones now, and it's a total pain anyway. You gotta clock in and out on it, but if you don't have a good signal out on the site, the little loading circle just spins and spins. We were working out at this new subdivision past the county line last week, and I swear, there is zero cell service out there. You have to walk all the way over to the porta-johns just to get one bar. And those porta-johns, man, when the sun beats down on them all afternoon? It's literally like a sauna in there. The blue chemical stuff they put in the bottom gets so hot it actually smells like burning plastic. The guys were complaining to the super about getting them cleaned out more than once a week, but you know how these big companies are, they just want to save a few bucks wherever they can. Like a couple months ago, they switched our work gloves from the good thick leather ones to these cheap synthetic ones that practically melt if you're grinding metal or doing any hot work... 

But, uh... wait, yeah. I just haven't been keeping up with my end of things. The paperwork and everything. My foreman is definitely noticing that I'm just not on top of it lately.

patient.answer:
Slowly? No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not doing much these days, but when I do move, it's just my regular speed. Definitely not as slow as this guy Gary on our crew, anyway. I swear that guy moves in actual slow motion. He's this older dude, always wears these bright neon green suspenders for some reason. 

He mostly just runs the skid steer, which is fine, but when he actually has to get out of the cab to help us move materials, it takes him like ten minutes just to climb down. We have a Bobcat T76 on site, the track loader one. It's actually a pretty sweet machine, way better than the wheeled ones if you're working in mud. The wheeled ones just spin out and get stuck the second it rains. Last spring we had this massive downpour and one of the new guys buried a wheeled John Deere loader straight up to the axles. We had to get an excavator just to pull him out, and we actually snapped a heavy-duty tow strap right in half doing it. It sounded like a literal gunshot when it snapped. You gotta be so careful with those straps, man, because if they snap and whip back at you, it'll break your leg easy. Or worse. My uncle actually lost his back window in his Chevy because a strap let go and the metal hook went right through the glass...

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Me moving slow? Yeah, no, my body feels fine. I'm just sitting around a lot more, that's all.

patient.answer:
No, I still enjoy things sometimes. Like, a good meal still tastes good, you know? I actually went to this taco truck down by the old armory a couple days ago. Best al pastor I've had in a long time. 

The guy who runs it is from Oaxaca, I think. He has this massive trompo set up right in the window, and he slices the pork right off it while it's spinning. He uses a real pineapple on top, too, none of that canned stuff. Canned pineapple is just way too sweet, it completely ruins the balance of the marinade. My ex-girlfriend used to put canned pineapple on her pizza, which, whatever, people like Hawaiian pizza, but she would put barbecue sauce on it instead of tomato sauce. It was the grossest thing I ever tasted. She'd order it from Domino's every Friday night, and I'd always just end up making myself a sandwich. I actually make a really good Italian sub. You gotta use the hard salami, not the cheap stuff, and you have to shred the lettuce super fine, like they do at Jersey Mike's. If you just put whole leaves of lettuce on a sub, it slides all over the place when you take a bite and makes a huge mess. Plus, you gotta hit it with the oil and vinegar right on the bread before you put the meat on...

But, uh... wait. Enjoying things? Yeah, I still like some things. I just don't have the energy to go do them much, but when I do, it's fine.

Down or hopeless? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm stressed out about the breakup and everything, and work is a mess, but I'm not, like, hopeless. I just feel kind of stuck right now, you know? Like I'm spinning my tires in the mud. 

Speaking of mud, you should have seen the site yesterday. We had that rain over the weekend, and the whole foundation trench for lot 42 completely washed out. The super was losing his mind. He had us out there with shovels trying to dig out the forms before the concrete trucks showed up. Mud is the absolute worst thing to shovel, man. It sticks to the metal, so every time you lift a scoop, it weighs like fifty pounds, and then half of it doesn't even slide off when you throw it. You have to keep banging the shovel against a rock just to clear it. I actually bought this special shovel a while back, a fiberglass handle one with a non-stick coating on the blade. Cost me like sixty bucks at Home Depot, which is insane for a shovel, but I figured it was an investment, right? Well, the very first week I brought it to the site, some idiot ran over the handle with a skid steer and snapped it clean in half. I was so mad. And of course, nobody fessed up to doing it. Just found it lying in the dirt next to the framing lumber...

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Hopeless? Yeah, no, I don't feel hopeless. Just, you know, dealing with a lot right now. I'm not down like that all the time.

Not getting things done? I mean, I guess I'm a little behind on some stuff, but it's not like I don't care. I'm just tired. Like, my apartment is a bit of a mess right now, but I'll get to it. I just haven't felt like doing laundry, mostly.

You have to run them twice just to get a load of jeans dry. I complained to the landlord about it, this guy Mr. Henderson. He's always wearing these golf shirts that are way too tight, and he just brushed me off. Said I was putting too many clothes in at once. Like, buddy, I know how to do laundry. My mom taught me how to separate the colors and everything. She used to be super strict about it. If a red sock got in with the whites, she'd lose her mind. She used this special stain remover spray that smelled like straight up chemicals, but it got everything out. I tried to find it at Target once, but I think they stopped making it because it probably caused cancer or something. Everything causes cancer now, right? I read this article online that said even the non-stick coating on pans is toxic. Which sucks, because I make eggs every morning. Well, not every morning lately, but I usually do. You gotta cook 'em low and slow if you want good scrambled eggs. If you blast the heat, they just get rubbery and gross. I usually throw some cheddar cheese in there, maybe some hot sauce...

But, uh... wait. What were we talking about? Motivation? Yeah, I mean, I'm doing okay. Just a little behind on chores, but I'm not, like, completely ignoring my life or anything. Work is still getting done, even if I'm not thrilled about being there.

Luckily it was empty, but it still dented the screen a little bit. Steve gets way too worked up about football. He plays in like three different fantasy leagues and he's always checking his phone during the game, complaining about how his tight end isn't getting enough targets. I tried doing fantasy football one year, but it's just too much work. You have to check the injury reports every week, and deal with the waiver wire... it's basically a second job. And my actual job is exhausting enough. Speaking of which, Steve owes me twenty bucks from a bet we made on the preseason, and he keeps dodging me about it. Like, dude, it's twenty bucks, just pay up. I know he has it, because he just bought this massive new truck. One of those F-250s with the lifted suspension. It's ridiculous, he doesn't even haul anything, he just drives it to his office job. Getting in and out of that thing is a workout...

But, uh... wait, what was the question? Nothing giving me pleasure? Yeah, no, I still enjoy stuff. I'm just, you know, tired a lot. But I still like things.

No, I don't think so. I mean, there hasn't been a day where literally *nothing* was interesting. Like, even on a bad day, I can still get into a good YouTube rabbit hole, you know? Then they carve a custom handle for it out of hickory or ash or something. I actually tried to carve a piece of wood once when I was a kid. I was sitting on the back porch trying to whittle a stick into a spear, and I ended up slicing my thumb open. Bled like crazy. She even used it to clean the bathroom grout, which actually worked pretty well. The bathroom always smelled like a hospital, though. 

But, uh... what were you asking? Days where nothing is enjoyable? No, I haven't had that. I mean, I'm stressed, but I still find stuff to do.

Low mood every day? Nah, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, I get bummed out sometimes, especially with everything going on lately, but it's not like an all-day, every-day kind of thing. My boss, Gary, he was screaming at the delivery driver on Tuesday. The driver's just this kid, probably barely eighteen, looking terrified. I felt bad for him, so I gave him a Gatorade from my cooler. It was the blue kind. Cool Blue, I think it's called? Best flavor by far. Though the yellow one is okay if you're really hungover. Not that I drink much anymore, but back when I was eighteen, me and my buddies used to drink those cheap 40-ounce malt liquors. We'd hang out behind the old abandoned roller rink... they tore it down a couple years ago to build a strip mall. Now there's a mattress store there. Who buys that many mattresses? There's a mattress store on like every corner. It's gotta be a front for something, right? Like money laundering or whatever. I saw this documentary on Netflix about money laundering... 

But, uh... what was I saying? Oh, being down all the time. No, I don't think so. I'm just stressed out, you know? But I still have okay days.

Loss of pleasure for most of the day? Nah, I don't think so. I mean, I told you about the YouTube videos, right? I still watch those. And I still like hanging out with my dog, Buster. I gave him half my turkey sandwich, and he just followed me around the rest of the day. My boss tried to chase him off, but Buster just hid under my truck. I took him home that night, and he's been with me ever since. He's got this weird habit, though. Every time the mail carrier comes, he doesn't bark, he just sits by the window and whines. Like a really high-pitched whine. It's so annoying. I tried training him out of it with those little training treats, the ones that smell like liver? But he just eats the treat and keeps whining. Dogs are weird, man. My neighbor's dog, this little yappy terrier thing, barks at literally everything. A leaf blows across the street? Bark. A squirrel looks at him funny? Bark. I don't know how they deal with it. I'd go crazy. 

But, uh... what did you ask me? Loss of interest? Yeah, no, I still care about stuff. I'm just worn out from work and everything else going on. But I still like doing things.

Man, I feel like we're going in circles here. Like I said, no, I haven't had days where nothing is enjoyable. I mean, I still like coming home and cracking open a beer on the porch. I usually get those cheap lagers, you know? Like PBR or Miller High Life. People talk trash about cheap beer, but honestly, after sweating on a roof for ten hours, it hits the spot way better than some fancy craft IPA that tastes like pine needles and grapefruit. My buddy Dave, he got super into homebrewing a few years ago. He bought all this equipment—kettles, carboys, hydrometers, the whole nine yards. He set it all up in his garage, which made his wife furious because she couldn't park her car in there during the winter. And winters here get brutal. Last year, we had that ice storm that knocked out the power for three days. I had to sleep in my Carhartt jacket and two pairs of socks. I tried to heat up a can of soup over a candle, which, let me tell you, does not work at all. It just gets the bottom of the can all black and sooty, and the soup stays freezing cold. I ended up just eating it cold anyway. It was chicken noodle. 

But yeah, what were we talking about? Oh, enjoying things. No, I still enjoy stuff. I'm just stressed, that's all. Not like... completely dead inside or anything.

patient.answer:
Unusually fatigued? Nah, not really. I mean, I'm beat at the end of the day, but I haul lumber and pour concrete for a living. It's not like I'm sitting on a couch feeling tired for no reason. We actually just finished this massive concrete pour on Wednesday. Concrete work is the worst, man. You gotta move so fast before it cures, especially when the sun is beating down on you. 

My coworker, Tommy, he actually dropped his phone right into the wet cement on that job. Just bloop, right in. It was one of those brand new phones too, the ones with the three cameras on the back. He tried to fish it out with his trowel, but it was completely encased by the time he got to it. Looked like a little gray brick. He was so mad he kicked the company truck and dented the fender. Boss was pissed, said he's taking it out of Tommy's paycheck. Which is kind of messed up, because the company trucks are already beat to hell anyway. The one I drive has a radio that only plays static, and the AC smells like old gym socks. I tried spraying Febreze in the vents last week, but it just made it smell like tropical gym socks. I don't even know what tropical is supposed to smell like anyway. Like coconuts? I hate coconut. The texture is awful, it's like chewing on wood shavings. Reminds me of hamster cages. I had a hamster when I was ten, named him Rex. He used to run on that squeaky wheel all night long... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Drop in energy? Yeah, no, my energy is fine. Just regular tired from working, that's all.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a loss of pleasure or interest in nearly all activities for most of the day, nearly every day in the past two weeks, which would support the diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder (F33.1).
doctor.question: Have you had days in the past two weeks where you felt like nothing was interesting or enjoyable for most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of interest or pleasure), which is not part of my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Are you asking me the same thing again? Man, I swear we just talked about this. No, I don't feel like nothing is enjoyable. Like I said, I still enjoy things. I still got my dog, I still got my beer. I mean, speaking of beer, I actually went to the store yesterday to get some, and the line was out the door. Just ridiculous. Turns out the lottery was up to like, what, 800 million or something? Everyone and their mother was buying tickets. I don't get the point, honestly. The odds of winning are worse than getting struck by lightning while getting eaten by a shark. But this one guy in front of me, he bought fifty bucks worth of scratch-offs. Just stood right there at the counter, scratching them with a quarter, holding up the whole line. The cashier looked like she wanted to die. She was this older lady, had those glasses on a chain around her neck, you know? She just kept sighing and looking at the ceiling. I felt bad for her, but I was also just trying to pay for my twelve-pack and go home. My feet were killing me. I need new boots. The steel toe on my left boot is starting to cut into my toes when I kneel down. I tried to find the same brand I bought last time, but the store at the mall closed down. Malls are so dead these days anyway. It's just empty storefronts and those weird kiosks selling phone cases... 

Anyway, look, I'm not sitting around hating everything, okay? I still like doing my usual stuff. I'm just stressed out.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant loss of pleasure or interest in activities for most of the day, nearly every day, over the past two weeks, which would help differentiate between F33.1 (Recurrent Depressive Disorder, current episode mild) and F43.22 (Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood).
doctor.question: Have you had days in the past two weeks where you felt like nothing was interesting or enjoyable for most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about anhedonia (loss of interest or pleasure), which is a symptom of major depressive disorder. My symptom profile for Adjustment Disorder does not include anhedonia.

patient.answer:
Dude, are you messing with me right now? You literally just asked me this, like, two seconds ago. And I already told you no, I still enjoy things. I'm not sitting around miserable all day. I mean, I was pretty miserable yesterday when my truck wouldn't start. The starter's been acting up for weeks, making this horrible grinding noise every time I turn the key. Sounds like metal chewing on metal. My buddy Carl told me I could just tap the starter with a hammer to get it going, but you try crawling under a Chevy in a gravel driveway when it's raining sideways. Gravel is the worst. My landlord refuses to pave the driveway. He says it's "rustic," but really he's just cheap. The guy drives a brand new Lexus but won't spend a dime on the property. Last month the hot water heater broke and it took him four days to send a guy out. Four days of taking freezing cold showers before work. It wakes you up, I'll give you that, but it's miserable. The plumber he finally sent was this kid who looked like he was barely out of high school. He had his pants sagging so low you could see his entire boxers. Plumber's crack is one thing, but this was a whole different level. He actually forgot his wrench and had to borrow mine. 

But seriously, doc, how many times are you gonna ask me the same question? No, I don't feel like nothing is enjoyable. Can we talk about something else now?

opening_question.intent: Identify the patient's chief complaint or reason for seeking psychiatric evaluation.
opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms are best explained by an adjustment disorder with depressed mood, given the clear temporal relationship between the onset of symptoms and a psychosocial stressor (moving into a problematic living situation). There is no evidence of a persistent low mood, anhedonia, or other core symptoms of major depressive disorder or recurrent depressive disorder.
